preDepartureTodos.labelHtml:
Pre-Departure To-Do

What to do when

Updated July 2026: deadlines separate tracking, refundable holds, and real booking windows so the list does not create false urgency a year out.

blocks.title: Track, do not panic-buy
blocks.note: Inventory opening is a search-alert trigger, not a cash-fare deadline.
items: Set fare alerts for the protected routing plus one acceptable fallback airport/routing.
Do not buy cash airfare just because seats opened; only grab award space or a fare already inside the trip budget with good flight times.
Track the open-jaw and Corfu-free exit alternatives; do not buy until car/ferry constraints are understood.

blocks.title: Hold scarce refundable stays
blocks.note: This is about protecting scarce family inventory, not chasing prepaid discounts.
items: Hold refundable Bonifacio and Sardinia family stays first; Bonifacio walkable rooms and Ogliastra beach bases are the tight inventory.
Keep cancellation buffers until the Corsica ferry and car plan are settled.

blocks.title: Cars, ferries, and route anchors
blocks.note: Use cancellable/pay-later terms where possible, then re-shop after flights are purchased.
items: Verify rental-car rules before villas; some contracts forbid taking an Italian rental into France/Corsica, so the default remains park-and-walk or separate transport.
Book the Sardinia-Corsica ferry early if taking a vehicle; for foot passengers, confirm schedule once 2027 sailings load (Corsica Ferries).

blocks.title: Buy flights in the real window
blocks.note: For peak-summer Europe, this is the practical cash-buy window: Google Flights puts U.S.-Europe fares near 94 days out, while Going gives 2-8 months for international trips and says to shift earlier for peak periods.
items: Buy when the total family fare and schedule both work; waiting for a theoretical bottom is not worth bad layovers or split seats.

blocks.title: Timed tickets and tours
blocks.note: These are the tasks with real external release windows or limited capacity.
items: Cala Goloritze reservations open 72 hours before visit and are capped, so set the exact reminder (Costa di Baunei).
La Pelosa access is controlled in season; standard places can open early, with most places released 2 days before at 09:00 (La Pelosa).
Book Gulf of Orosei boat days 30-60 days out and keep a wind backup.

blocks.title: Final checks
items: Passports: Schengen requires validity 3+ months after planned EU departure and issue within the last 10 years (EU); renew before winter if anyone is close.
ETIAS: no July 2026 action; the U.S. State Dept. says ETIAS is planned for late 2026, so apply only after the official system launches (State Dept.).
Insurance: compare family medical/trip coverage after the first meaningful deposit; waiver timing is policy-specific, so do not wait until final payment if coverage matters.
Re-check ferry strikes, mistral/wind, and beach access rules during the final week.

preDepartureTodos.callout: Why this no longer says "act now" for flights: airline seats may become searchable about 11 months out, but that is not the cheapest cash-buy signal. Expedia 2026 Air Hacks found 180+ day bookings were the most expensive category in its data; Going puts international trips in a 2-8 month window, and Google Flights says U.S.-Europe trips cluster around 94 days out with risk rising inside 50 days. Track now, buy early only for award seats, unusually good protected routing, or a fare already inside budget.

*{box-sizing:border-box}

 font:16px/1.55 "Inter",ui-sans-serif,system-ui,-apple-system,"Segoe UI",sans-serif;-webkit-font-smoothing:antialiased}

/* HERO */

 background:linear-gradient(180deg,rgba(10,20,24,.12),rgba(10,18,22,.34) 45%,rgba(8,14,18,.88)),url("../../assets/img/sardinia-corsica/google_alghero_bastioni_01.jpg") center 40% / cover;transform:scale(1.03);z-index:-1}

.hero-meta{display:flex;flex-wrap:wrap;gap:26px}

/* NAV */

.site-nav{z-index:500;--nav-bg:#17130f;--nav-panel:#211c16;--nav-panel-2:#2a231b;--nav-line:rgba(246,241,231,.16);--nav-text:#f6f1e7;--nav-muted:rgba(246,241,231,.62);--nav-active:#5f9aa3;--nav-active-ink:#061517;--nav-shadow:0 18px 42px rgba(12,10,8,.28)}
.site-nav summary{list-style:none}
.site-nav summary::-webkit-details-marker{display:none}

}
@media(max-width:959px){
  .site-nav{position:sticky;top:0;padding:10px clamp(14px,4vw,22px);background:rgba(23,19,15,.96);border-bottom:1px solid var(--nav-line);backdrop-filter:blur(14px);box-shadow:0 10px 28px rgba(12,10,8,.18)}
  .site-nav-menu{max-width:1320px;margin:0 auto}
  .site-nav summary{display:flex;align-items:center;justify-content:space-between;gap:14px;min-height:42px;padding:8px 12px;border:1px solid var(--nav-line);border-radius:10px;background:var(--nav-panel);box-shadow:0 8px 24px rgba(12,10,8,.22);color:var(--nav-text);font-size:.84rem;font-weight:900;cursor:pointer}
  .site-nav summary::after{content:"+";display:grid;place-items:center;width:24px;height:24px;border-radius:50%;background:var(--nav-active);color:var(--nav-active-ink);font-size:1rem;line-height:1}
  .site-nav-menu[open] summary{border-color:rgba(95,154,163,.55)}
  .site-nav-menu[open] summary::after{content:"-"}
  .site-nav-links{display:grid;grid-template-columns:repeat(auto-fit,minmax(145px,1fr));gap:7px;margin-top:8px;max-height:min(70vh,480px);overflow:auto;padding:8px;border:1px solid var(--nav-line);border-radius:12px;background:linear-gradient(180deg,var(--nav-panel),var(--nav-bg));box-shadow:0 18px 42px rgba(12,10,8,.34)}
  .site-nav a{display:flex;align-items:center;min-height:42px;padding:9px 10px;border:1px solid var(--nav-line);border-radius:8px;background:rgba(246,241,231,.06);font-size:.82rem}
  .site-nav a.nav-home,.site-nav a:hover{background:var(--nav-active);color:var(--nav-active-ink);border-color:var(--nav-active)}
}

.tips-order li::before{content:counter(step);position:absolute;left:6px;top:50%;transform:translateY(-50%);width:18px;height:18px;border-radius:50%;background:var(--c1);color:#fff;font-size:.68rem;font-weight:800;display:grid;place-items:center}

.tcard.later .tlabel{background:var(--c2)}
.tcard h4{margin:0 0 12px;font-size:1.25rem;font-weight:600}
.tcard .trow{display:flex;justify-content:space-between;gap:14px;padding:7px 0;border-bottom:1px solid var(--line);font-size:.88rem}
.tcard .trow:last-child{border-bottom:0}
.tcard .trow span{color:var(--muted)}

.verdict-box h4{margin:0 0 8px;font-size:1.1rem;font-weight:800}

.verdict-box p:last-child{margin-bottom:0}

.tripmap-wrap{background:var(--card);border:1px solid var(--line);border-radius:20px;padding:14px;box-shadow:var(--shadow)}

.leaflet-popup-content{font:14px/1.4 "Inter",sans-serif}

.pin{width:16px;height:16px;border-radius:50%;border:2.5px solid #fff;box-shadow:0 1px 5px rgba(0,0,0,.5)}

Air Travel

North in, Cagliari out

There is no Pittsburgh–Sardinia nonstop and no US nonstop to any Sardinian airport, so every option connects through one European hub (Rome, Munich, Frankfurt, Paris, London). The open-jaw — land near the Alghero base, depart from the Cagliari base — saves a long backtracking drive on the last day. A 2026 fare check ran roughly $608–701 per person; budget the four-seat total in the $3,200–4,600 band and re-quote about 11 months out.

What People Are Saying

Insider field notes

Crowd-sourced from Reddit, TripAdvisor forums, and local-run Sardinia/Corsica blogs (2026) — the honest, off-the-brochure stuff. Reconfirm access rules, ferry times, and beach caps when 2027 inventory opens.

  • Alghero & La Pelosa

    Warm water, but the famous beach is capped

    • La Pelosa now sells timed tickets and caps daily numbers. In summer you must pre-book online, pay a few euro per adult, and bring a mat (no bags directly on the sand). Book the morning slot before it sells out.
    • The sea actually is that shallow and clear. Repeat praise: waist-deep turquoise a long way out, genuinely warm by mid-June — the single biggest reason families rate Sardinia over cooler Atlantic coasts.
    • Sleep just outside Alghero's ZTL and walk in. Old-town driving is restricted and camera-enforced; park outside and stroll the Bastioni seawall at sunset.

  • Bonifacio, Corsica

    Worth the ferry — plan the logistics

    • Do it as a foot-passenger day trip. Forum consensus: don't try to ferry your Sardinian rental over — most contracts ban leaving Italy. Walk on, and the cliff-top citadel is an easy, jaw-dropping stroll from the port.
    • Climb (or don't) the King of Aragon stairway. 187 steep steps cut into the cliff; the view is unreal but it's a lot in the heat for little legs — the citadel lanes above are the low-effort payoff.
    • Rondinara is the family beach. Shallow, sheltered horseshoe bay north of town; a short taxi/drive if you've arranged Corsica-side wheels.

  • Cala Goloritzè

    The signature hike, respected honestly

    • It's a real hike, not a stroll. ~45–60 min down a rocky trail and the same back up in full sun; people underestimate the climb out. Start early, carry water, and this is a water-shoes / real-shoes day.
    • Access is capped and ticketed. The beach limits daily entries and you generally reserve ahead — check the current permit system before driving to the trailhead.
    • The reward is the payoff. Near-universal "most beautiful beach we've seen" reviews for the limestone pinnacle and clear cold-clear water — kids swim once they're down.

  • Gulf of Orosei by boat

    The premium day, and why it's worth it

    • The best coves are basically boat-only. Cala Mariolu, Cala Biriala and friends have little or no road access — a boat or guided dinghy from Santa Maria Navarrese / Arbatax is the realistic family way in.
    • Book a small-group or private tour, not the big cattle boat. Repeated advice: the mega-boats dump 200 people on one cove at noon; a smaller charter hits two or three coves and beats the crowd.
    • Bring reef shoes. These are white-pebble beaches, not sand — gorgeous, but hard on bare feet getting in and out.

  • Cagliari & Poetto

    An easy, underrated finish

    • Poetto is a long, calm, family-easy city beach. Kilometres of shallow sand reachable by bus from town, with lidos, showers, and cheap kiosks — a low-drama last-days base after all the driving.
    • The flamingos are real and free. The Molentargius wetland behind Poetto holds pink flamingos year-round; an easy walk/bike the kids love, no ticket needed.
    • Villasimius for one more knockout beach. Porto Giunco / Simius are the "save one great beach for last" pick; go early for parking, or swap in Nora's seaside Roman ruins if you want ruins-plus-swim.
